LESSON: MAGNETISM AND ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Natural Physical Science
Topic 3.4: Magnetism and electromagnetic induction
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Magnetism and electromagnetic induction, part of Natural Physical Science in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How is the study of electromagnetic induction important in our daily life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Magnetism and electromagnetic induction together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: as the learner designs and makes a simple electric bell using locally available materials.

● Learning to learn: as the learner carries out experiments of magnetising a magnetic material and demagnetizing a

magnet.

Values:
● Unity: as the learner carries out assigned roles when carrying out experiments to demonstrate electromagnetic

induction.

● Responsibility: as the learner takes care of the apparatus (U-shaped magnet, galvanometer and straight conductors)

while carrying out experiments on electromagnetic induction.

65

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills; Self-esteem: as the learner explains the methods of magnetization and demagnetization.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Print textbooks in appropriate font and colour,

● Braille textbooks,

● Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers and screen magnifiers,

● Real objects like U-shaped magnet, galvanometer and straight conductors e.t.c

Key Skills:

● Performing an experiment on electromagnetic induction.

● Describing the magnetic field patterns around a magnet.

• Describing induced electromotive force in electromagnetism.
